description: Raw-value predicate expansion — expand g_i shorthand into threshold comparisons on resolved_* fields (e.g. g_r(r,kappa)==CAUTION becomes resolved_r_rate>10 AND resolved_r_rate<=20 AND resolved_r_kappa==0)
preserves_layer_boundary: NO — Layer 3 recomputes the classification that Layer 2 already made
duplicates_layer2_logic: YES — directly copies threshold structure from g_r/g_o/g_w into Layer 3
changes_scientific_semantics: YES — identical semantics claimed but implemented twice; divergence risk
supports_existing_rules: PARTIAL — R-CAUTION-001 already implemented without Model A; Model A needed only for 002/003/004
preserves_exclusion_semantics: PARTIAL — can represent None as evaluation failure but loses EXCLUDED distinction
preserves_fault_semantics: PARTIAL — g_i(bottom)=UNSAFE is bypassed; Layer 3 sees None and must independently classify
implementation_complexity: HIGH — per-vessel predicate sets for g_o; two-input logic for g_r; threshold constants duplicated
scientific_risk: HIGH — threshold drift between layers; semantic divergence; duplication violates layer boundary principle
rationale: Layer 3 would perform the exact computation that Layer 2 already performed. Thresholds 21.6/27.0 (g_w) and 10.0/20.0 (g_r) and vessel-specific wave bands (g_o) are Layer 2 classifier properties. Copying them into Layer 3 violates the frozen architecture boundary (task §4). Any future threshold change must be made in both layers (divergence risk). kappa semantics would also need to be reflected in Layer 3 rainfall predicates.

description: Layer 2 component-state interface — Layer 2 exposes already-computed g_i(.) outputs as ComponentStateTrace alongside S; Layer 3 predicates consume these classified results
preserves_layer_boundary: YES — Layer 2 computes g_i(.) once; Layer 3 consumes results only; no threshold logic in Layer 3
duplicates_layer2_logic: NO — Layer 3 reads a result not a computation; thresholds remain inside Layer 2
changes_scientific_semantics: NO — scientific semantics of each rule antecedent preserved (g_o==CAUTION is still g_o==CAUTION)
supports_existing_rules: YES — R-CAUTION-002/003/004 become directly executable; R-CAUTION-001 consistency path available as future migration
preserves_exclusion_semantics: YES — excluded components represented as EXCLUDED (distinct from SAFE/CAUTION); m in D gives m_state=EXCLUDED
preserves_fault_semantics: YES — faulted components cause S=UNSAFE which gate-offs Layer 3; UNSAFE component states never visible to Layer 3
implementation_complexity: MEDIUM — interface extension to DecisionContext; layer3-prototype-spec §7 provision already exists
scientific_risk: LOW — no duplication; Safety Dominance proof unaffected (depends only on S); layer3-prototype-spec §7 anticipates this
decision: ACCEPTED for R-CAUTION-002/003/004 — pending Batch 4B canonical update and implementation
rationale: Layer 2 g_i(.) computations are internal intermediate results of computing S. Exposing them is making an already-existing internal result explicit — the computation already happened. The Safety Dominance proof (Appendix C §C.7.2 Theorem C.3) depends only on the value of S not on additional interface data. Exclusion semantics preserved by EXCLUDED value. Fault semantics preserved by UNSAFE gate-off. Canonical change required: architecture-illustration.md must be updated before Batch 4B implementation. Implementation authorised in principle pending that update.

description: Explanatory cause interface — use reasons taxonomy (fault/hazard/policy) or component-level provenance to select rules
preserves_layer_boundary: NO — reasons are explicitly defined as explanatory-only annotations (Appendix C §C.2.0.8); using them to select rules converts annotations into decision authority
duplicates_layer2_logic: YES — reasons are derived from g_i outputs; using them for rule selection indirectly uses Layer 2 classification through a semantic proxy
changes_scientific_semantics: YES — reasons must never govern (task §16; Appendix C §C.2.0.8 explicit prohibition)
supports_existing_rules: NO — no existing rule antecedents are expressed in terms of reasons; they use g_i state shorthand
preserves_exclusion_semantics: UNCLEAR — reasons taxonomy does not distinguish EXCLUDED from SAFE or CAUTION
preserves_fault_semantics: NO — fault reason exists but using it in rule selection governs on fault state
implementation_complexity: LOW — reasons already produced by Layer 2
scientific_risk: HIGH — fundamentally misuses the explanatory/architectural distinction; violates the provenance contract
rationale: The canonical architecture prohibits using reasons as decision inputs. This is stated in three places: Appendix C §C.2.0.8 (reasons are annotations only and never participate in governance); Appendix C §C.7.2 (reasons cannot select RS(S)); and task §16. Model C is architecturally prohibited regardless of implementation feasibility.

description: Keep all deferred — no interface change; Batch 3 engine operates with R-CAUTION-001 only
supports_existing_rules: PARTIAL — R-CAUTION-001 remains the only executable rule
scientific_risk: NONE for architecture; HIGH for replay activation (R-CAUTION-001 produces 0 activations when m in D)
decision: PARTIAL — accepted for R-SAFE-001 (STATE_RESTATEMENT); not accepted for R-CAUTION-002/003/004 where Model B is available
rationale: Full deferral of R-CAUTION-002/003/004 is scientifically acceptable (task §6) but unnecessary when Model B provides a clean path. Retaining all four rules as deferred would mean F1-F3 evaluate an engine with only R-CAUTION-001 which produces zero activations in the replay (m in D). R-SAFE-001 should remain deferred due to STATE_RESTATEMENT regardless of model choice.
